Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/theme-generator (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

hue.summary: The generator's own hue; unset, the colour's

chroma.summary: The generator's own chroma; unset, the colour's

swatches.summary: The product's colours beside the picker, as sf-color takes them: #hex|Name, #hex

apply.summary: Put the theme on target as inline variables at every change; without it the page is not changed

target.summary: A CSS selector of the element apply themes; empty, the document's root

selector.summary: The rule's selector in the events and in toCSS()

theme.summary: The theme shown now (simai.framework.theme.v1), a copy

change.summary: The choice changed -- a drag in the picker, a swatch, a number typed (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5.1: sf-theme-change → change on the theme generator); the browser's name, with the theme in the detail

committed.summary: The choice was committed -- the picker's change, a swatch, Enter or leaving a field, Reset: the theme the host keeps

reset.summary: Back to SIMAI Framework's own colour; a committed choice

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The generator is a group named by its aria-label or the language file's runtime.title; its controls are sf-color (the main colour), two sf-input number fields in a <details> and an sf-button, each with its own name; the preview is a section named «Предпросмотр темы» whose swatches are images named by palette, tone and hex. Enter in a field commits.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-theme-generator for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: the vocabulary's change; the alias table's sf-theme-generator-change (2026-10-18) is itself dated now
rows.summary: The choice moved: a drag across the picker, a swatch, a number typed in a field.

rows.note: the first name (journal event-theme-generator-names); the Loader's light/dark event bears the same name
rows.summary: Its first name, still emitted with the same detail until 2026-12-01 (journal event-theme-generator-names); the Loader's light/dark event bears it too. Bind sf-theme-generator-change.

rows.note: the commit is a fact; apply is the vocabulary's action on entries
rows.summary: The choice was committed: the picker's change, a swatch, Enter or leaving a field, Reset.
Its first name, still emitted with the same detail until 2026-12-01 (journal event-theme-generator-names); the Loader's light/dark event bears it too. Bind sf-theme-generator-apply.

x-summary: A theme from one colour: the main colour, the generator's own hue and chroma, a preview of the four theme palettes and a way back to SIMAI Framework's colour; it stores nothing and changes the page only with apply.
x-renamed: events.sf-theme-generator-change and its first name sf-theme-change → change (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5.1: sf-theme-change → change on the theme generator); both dated same-detail aliases

events.sf-theme-generator-apply and its first name sf-theme-apply → committed: the choice was committed, a fact (the vocabulary's apply is an action on entries, {action, scope}, not this); both dated same-detail aliases
settings hue, chroma: strings → numbers, nullable (§16 item 29)
methods toCSS(), toJSON(): reads of the value theme, kept as methods; reset() is the action reset
x-decisions: assembly: a leaf, with reasons. It draws sf-color, two sf-input fields and an sf-button, but they are the controls of its own one value -- the colour, and the hue and chroma that tune it -- with no data or rule between them beyond the calculation the element makes; written as an assembly it would gain keys, roles and bindings for nothing it does. The parts are migrated (the fields family) and it uses them through their public interface.

alias-conflict: the alias table's sf-theme-change → sf-theme-generator-change (shipped 2026-10-18, journal event-theme-generator-names) and this conversion's change -- the vocabulary decides (1.1.5 §5.1, sf-theme-change → change on the theme generator): the event is the browser's change, with the theme in the detail, and both sf-theme-generator-change and sf-theme-change follow it with the same detail until 2026-12-01. As before, it is sent at every change of the choice, not only at the commit.

the commit is committed (a fact, the past form, its word in the language files): sf-theme-generator-committed. The vocabulary's apply is an action on entries {action, scope}, so the old name would have read as that verb with another payload; sf-theme-generator-apply and sf-theme-apply follow with the same detail until 2026-12-01. The setting apply (whether the theme is put on the page) keeps its name: a setting, not an event.
hue and chroma are numbers (integer, nullable, 0–360 and 0–150): unset, the colour's reading; out of range they read at the edge, as before.
reset is the action (answers applied); toCSS(selector) and toJSON() stay methods: they read the value theme and change nothing, which is no action (§4.4).
a11y-name: the generator is a group named by its aria-label, else the language file's runtime.title («Генератор темы», "Theme generator"); its root carries role group.
key-effects: Tab reaches its controls; Enter in a number field commits (commit), without submitting a form around it.
words (§11): the language files' runtime words, read with sfWord; THEME_TEXT is gone (hueHint and chromaHint are hue-hint and chroma-hint).
version 1.1.0: events renamed behind dated aliases, hue and chroma typed (§4.10).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (a green theme) plus SIMAI Framework's colour, a tuned hue and chroma, product swatches and apply to a part of the page.
css-variables: five public variables of its sheet: the gap, the text's ink, the labels' ink, the swatches' radius and border. Listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.
source-drift: the shipped manifest differs from 5100227 in the alias rows and its provenance; the interface converted is the shipped one.

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 1.1.2: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.4: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.8 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.9 information-steps: a theme carries 232 variables -- 128 tones and 104 translucent steps -- since the core's information palette has its state steps (C16 S1: info-50 at 4/8, info-90 at 4/8/12/24, written by THEME_ALPHA). The documented counts follow; the generator's API is unchanged.
version 1.1.10: the first-paint snapshot is retaken: a nested sized component now carries data-sf-size-relative at first paint (density C22, core.runtime 1.45.0); nothing it draws changes.

version 1.1.11 static-palette (one above the released 1.1.10): core theme-palette.js also holds the static palette (owner decision C17, 2026-11-08): STATIC_HUES, staticPalette() and staticVariables(), and the four status rules are read from their hues (error red, warning amber, success green, info blue) by the same numbers. A theme this element makes is byte for byte the same; settings, values, events and keys unchanged. A theme carries 288 variables -- 128 tones and 160 translucent steps -- since tone 20 has its steps 4 to 24, 64 and 80 on the seven coloured palettes (C16 coloured places, dispatcher 2026-11-09).

version 1.1.12 (2026-11-09): a patch; nothing in the component changed. The sf-input it draws asks for the kbd sheet since sf-input 1.7.0 (C38, the shortcut setting; component.kbd 1.3.0), so its first-paint snapshots name that sheet and carry one more empty line where the field's shortcut would stand; the component takes a patch with them. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.1.13 (2026-11-11): one reset for one action (docs pre-check 2026-11-10 TG-02): the colour field's own inherited reset is not drawn beside «Сбросить»; the colour field draws its own label (sf-input-color 1.6.0), so the generator's copy of it is gone. Its events were already change and sf-theme-generator-committed, the former names dated aliases (TG-01 is the page's).

version 1.1.14 (2026-11-11): the information palette is the static hue sky (owner decision C17 as amended 2026-11-11: info is not blue, or it reads as the Framework's own primary); core STATUS_HUES info is sky, so the generator's «Информация» row and every theme it writes carry sky's tones (tone 40 is sky's, --sf-sky-40, where it was blue's). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.0 (2026-11-12) TG-01: a theme is the four dynamic palettes -- primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral -- and no status palette. Core declares error, warning, success and info as var() of the static hues red, amber, green and sky (C17, C90), and a theme that wrote them as literal colours froze them at the day it was made: after core moved info to sky, a page themed by the generator kept the old blue. The theme value, toJSON(), toCSS() and the events' theme, variables and css now hold 144 variables (64 tones, 80 translucent steps), where they held 288; the preview has four rows, not eight (the status rows never moved, docs study R132 TG-06). A theme object stored before (eight palettes) applies only its four theme palettes. Settings, events and keys unchanged; journal behaviour-theme-writes-no-status-palette.

$comment: The generator draws a colour control, two number fields and a reset button;
a tag it renders is a tag it fetches, with the icons they show.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-theme-generator where a person chooses a site's or a product's main colour and the rest of its palette should follow.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not copy the palette calculation; import core theme-palette
Do not expect the component to store the choice; the host keeps it

accessibility.focus: The colour control, Reset, the «Advanced» disclosure and its two number fields are in the focus order; Enter in a field commits the theme. The preview is a named region of labelled swatches, each giving its palette, tone and hex.
